condition.reference: Navamsa occupied by the lord of the tenth house

normalized_rule: The source maps the Navamsa occupied by the lord of the tenth house to a vocation: Sun to fruit cultivation, mantra, fraud/gambling/falsehood, wool, medicine, metals, or service; Moon to water products, agriculture, cattle, pilgrimage, or cloth; Mars to metals, battle, cooking, land, weapons, adventure, or associated low-vocation imagery; Mercury to composition, scripture study, scribal or clerical work, astrology, mantra, or priesthood; Jupiter to Brahmins, gods, royal favor, religious study, preaching, or lending money; Venus to women, livestock, music, luxury goods, or courtly/poetic roles; and Saturn to roots and fruits, manual labor, servants, sculpture, wood, or explicitly low-status trades in the cited passage.
synthesis_notes: The source's occupational categories are historically situated and must not be presented as a complete or universally applicable labor taxonomy.
review_notes: The table is retained as one source lookup rule; outcome catalogues and ethical judgments are not generalized into modern career advice.
transmission_notes: The 1937 Sastri English translation is used as a reference-only source layer.
